title: Solved risk-based guardrail balance thresholds
meaning: The cut and raise portfolio levels the risk-based guardrail solver finds for the plan's success band, as a fraction of today's investable portfolio: for each band edge, the lowest point of the solver's ten-step bisection lattice on [0.02, 4] whose fixed-target Monte Carlo success on shared seeded paths is at or above that edge.

surfaces.selector: Spending card, risk-based guardrails callout "cut spending if the portfolio falls below $X; raise if it rises above $Y" (SpendingPolicyRiskBased.tsx RiskBasedThresholdsCallout)
Risk-based spending guardrails callout "if the portfolio falls below $X ... above $Y"
Risk-based dollar guardrails note "cut below $X · raise above $Y (today's dollars, solved on Spending)"

transformations: The solver publishes balancePct = round(balanceFrac × 10,000) / 100 (montecarlo/riskBasedGuardrails.ts#balanceThresholdPct), which useThresholdSolve persists into plan.expenses.spendingPolicy.lowerBalanceThresholdPct / upperBalanceThresholdPct; guardrailThresholdDollars prints it in dollars (family display-guardrail-balance-thresholds).
notes: Solved on demand (Spending card button) under the lognormal model at 12% volatility around the plan's own expected returns (allocated accounts use their asset classes' volatilities), with 200 paths and the engine's default seed (DEFAULT_MONTE_CARLO_SEED, the same for every plan; before decision D-MC-DEFAULT-SEED of 2026-09-28 it was a hash of the plan id), whatever model the Monte Carlo page shows; the seed is stored beside the thresholds, and thresholds saved without one were solved on the plan-id seed, which the Spending card says. The persisted percents also drive the projection's guardrail rule (spending/guardrails.ts: cut below lowerBalanceThresholdPct/100 x the starting real portfolio, raise above upper), so the value feeds spending-guardrail-factor-annual and monte-carlo-guardrail-action-counts. RiskBasedThreshold.balanceDollars (the fraction times the balance, which never acted) was removed in B2-P1 slice 2; the printed dollars are the persisted percent of today's balances. 'assumptions-card' stands in for the Spending card, which has no surface name in the vocabulary (the census's household-section gap).

title: Suggested spending adjustment at a solved guardrail threshold
meaning: The monthly spending cut at the solved cut threshold, or raise at the solved raise threshold, that brings fixed-target Monte Carlo success back to the middle of the band: |1 − m| × base annual spending / 12, with m the eight-step bisection result for the spending multiplier.

surfaces.selector: Spending card, risk-based guardrails callout "trimming about $X/mo restores the middle of the band" / "roughly $Y/mo of extra spending" (SpendingPolicyRiskBased.tsx RiskBasedThresholdsCallout)

notes: Rendered only from the in-memory solution of the latest solve; it is not persisted in the plan. When even a 2x raise keeps success above the midpoint the raise is reported at the bracket maximum (m = 2).
